Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
sharks %>% 
  count(county,sort = T) %>% 
  head(5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   county            n
##   <chr>         <int>
## 1 San Diego        25
## 2 Humboldt         20
## 3 San Mateo        19
## 4 Santa Barbara    19
## 5 Marin            16
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=county, fill = county))+
  geom_bar()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "Shark Related Incidents Per Coastal California County",
       x="County",
       y=NULL)

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  select(month) %>% 
  mutate(month=as.factor(month)) %>%
  mutate(month=recode(month,
                      "1"="january",
                      "2"="febuary",
                      "3"="march",
                      "4"="april",
                      "5"="may",
                      "6"="june",
                      "7"="july",
                      "8"="augest",
                      "9"="september",
                      "10"="october",
                      "11"="november",
                      "12"="december")) %>%
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=month,fill= month))+
  geom_bar()+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "Number of Shark Related injuies in CA Per Month of Year",
       x="Month",
       y="Total Injuries")

#October has the most incidents a year, there is a trend that the late summer and fall months have the most incidents
  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  select(time) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x=time))+
  geom_bar()+
  coord_flip()+
  theme(text=element_text(size=8))+
  labs(title = "Number of Shark Related Injuires in CA per Time of Day",
       x="Time",
       y="Total Injuries")

#11 Am is when the most attacks occur
  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format)
sharks2 <- sharks %>% 
  select(county,injury) %>% 
  mutate(injury=as.factor(injury)) %>% 
  group_by(county, injury) %>% 
  summarise(count = n()) %>% 
  summarise(total=sum(count))
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'county'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
sharks2
## # A tibble: 22 × 2
##    county                 total
##    <chr>                  <int>
##  1 Del Norte                  3
##  2 Humboldt                  20
##  3 Island - Catalina          4
##  4 Island - Farallones        7
##  5 Island - San Miguel        5
##  6 Island - San Nicolas       1
##  7 Island - Santa Barbara     1
##  8 Island - Santa Cruz        2
##  9 Island - Santa Rosa        1
## 10 Los Angeles               10
## # ℹ 12 more rows
# San Diego has the most injuries
#I dont understand why this table needs to be in wide format when long does the same?
  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.
sharks2 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=county, y=total)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = county))+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "Number of Shark Related Injuires Per CA County",
       x="County",
       y="Total Injuries")

  1. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents?
sharks3 <- sharks %>% 
  select(mode,injury) %>% 
  mutate(injury=as.factor(injury)) %>% 
  group_by(mode, injury) %>% 
  summarise(count = n()) %>% 
  summarise(total=sum(count))
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'mode'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
sharks3
## # A tibble: 8 × 2
##   mode                total
##   <chr>               <int>
## 1 Freediving             36
## 2 Hookah Diving          10
## 3 Kayaking / Canoeing    30
## 4 Paddleboarding          7
## 5 Scuba Diving           20
## 6 Surfing / Boarding     85
## 7 Swimming               22
## 8 Walking in shallow      1
#Surfing has the highest number of shark injuries
  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks3 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=mode, y=total)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = mode))+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "Number of Shark Related Injuries Based On Activity",
       x="Activity",
       y="Total Injuries")

  1. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
sharks4 <- sharks %>% 
  select(species,injury) %>% 
  mutate(injury=as.factor(injury)) %>% 
  group_by(species, injury) %>% 
  summarise(count = n()) %>% 
  summarise(total=sum(count))
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'species'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.

#Great Whites are responsibe for the highest number of injuries
  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
sharks %>% 
  select(species,injury) %>% 
  filter(species=="White") %>% 
  mutate(injury=as.factor(injury)) %>% 
  group_by(species, injury) %>% 
  summarise(count=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=injury, y=count))+
  geom_col(aes(fill = injury)) +
  labs(title = "Type of Injury related to Great White Incidents",
       x="Injury Type",
       y="Total Injuries")
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'species'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.

#Not all Great White incidents are fatal but the ones that do occur leave either no injury or major injury
